CLOSED 2026-08-26 in caa46c6 — Phase 30 requirement 4. A revived socket is CLOSED with 1012, not resumed: Noise has no session resumption and yamux no resync, so every alternative is a connection that lies about being live. The registry is keyed by socket identity, so the miss IS the detection. FIVE PLANTS WATCHED RED. The route is wired, so createHostedFabric has a production caller — bundle 583.94 -> 1867.80 KiB, kadDHT 0 -> 11, and diffieHellman/node:crypto STILL 0. §17's claim is deliberately narrowed in the prose: yamux defaults enableKeepAlive at 30 s, so an object under a live connection will not hibernate at all and the proven win is only the six-minute abort. TAMING THE KEEPALIVE IS A NAMED OPEN DECISION, NOT TAKEN — a peer that never sends cannot detect a dead path. Also open and reported: whether workerd accepts 1012 (1011 is known accepted), and whether binaryType may be assigned on a hibernatable socket, deliberately not asserted either way. Phase 30 criteria 1-3 need >5 distinct clients against a deployed node and stay owner acts.

CLOSED 2026-08-26 in 2aa0a6b — the ninth mode has a CAUSE, proven by planting rather than by waiting. The solo owner’s shard has exactly one legal executor (sovereign, its owner, REDUNDANCY 1, nothing may be duplicated for it) so its only exit is the thaw; delay the thaw past RPC_TIMEOUT_MS and the single dispatch fails on that budget with no untried node behind it, ending no-untried-node and reading null at index 21. At 5 000 ms every shard still agreed; at 15 000 ms the frozen dispatches capped at 10001/10001/10000 ms and #21 came back "rpc to ... timed out after 10000ms". THAT IS THE FABRIC BEHAVING CORRECTLY — nothing in production to repair; what was defective is the fixture’s silence about resting on freeze-to-release staying inside the budget. NO NEW ASSERTION, and the reason is measured: the solo dispatch begins after freeze() resolves, so a bound on the span would redden a green run in a ~200 ms band. The span is printed instead. THE PLANT CAUGHT A DEFECT IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT — the first version read thawedAt, the instant the thaw is DECIDED, and printed 764 ms under a 15 000 ms delay; now taken at releasedAt, reading 1381 ms clean and 16 244 ms planted. NOT REPRODUCED NATURALLY in ten runs under eight CPU burners at load 16-50, and no frequency is claimed.

CLOSED 2026-08-26 in 6868139 — ShardResult.judgedAt is published by the scheduler from its own `woke`, threaded exactly parallel to `speculated`, and the fixture READS it instead of reconstructing it. THE FINDING IS THAT THE BIAS IS SMALLER THAN THE CLAIM THAT ASKED FOR THE FIELD: the handoff said the window admits "exactly the dispatches running alongside the duplicates, the slowest in the job", which was reasoning; six runs (one quiet, five under eight CPU burners at load 162-184) put it at 0-2 ms holding 0 dispatches EVERY TIME. So the field is not a repair of an observed defect — it is a number read where it was inferred, and both are printed so the day the window holds something the run says so. THE CLOCK BASIS IS THE TRAP AND IT IS REAL: JobClock defaults to Date.now() (epoch) while the wrapper log is performance.now(); the fixture converts once by performance.timeOrigin. Plant P3 printed "expected 1787789701143 to be null", which is that basis confirming itself. Three plants watched red — merge dropped, woke+10_000, published at the eligibility gate — and the invariant is closed on BOTH sides in one run. No codec: no .proto in the tree, ShardResult is requestor-local. Blast radius 4 fixture literals, enumerated by tsc rather than grep.

A TENTH speculation-agents mode. INSTRUMENT LANDED 2026-08-26 in 4909617, CAUSE STILL UNVERIFIED and deliberately so. The symptom: `on.shards.flatMap(s => s.rejections)` came back with one `unreachable: no answer in 2000ms`, seen once in ten runs under eight CPU burners at load 29. It could not be attributed because the fixture printed no frozen ids, and the two readings it could not separate are OPPOSITE — the fixture’s own freeze reaching the admission-offer path (a fixture defect) versus a genuine reading about that path under load. Each refusal now prints the ROLE of the node that gave it: FROZEN(public-victim), FROZEN(paired-owner), FROZEN(solo-owner), FROZEN(unclassified) or healthy. Two plants watched red, one per branch. NOT REPRODUCED SINCE: twelve further runs under eight burners at load up to 235 stayed green, so across both hunts it is ONE redness in TWENTY-TWO runs, and LOAD IS NOT ESTABLISHED AS THE VARIABLE and must not be written down as the cause. CORRECTED 2026-08-26, same day: 4909617’s message says "the single hit came at load 29 while eighteen runs above it were green" and THAT FIGURE IS NOT DEFENSIBLE — per-run load readings exist only for the first hunt (15.95, 29.00 RED, 29.93, 36.01, 41.25, 49.91, 49.37, 49.88, 50.69, 48.90, each taken AFTER its run), while the second hunt recorded only a final 235.70 and began on fresh burners, so an unknown number of its twelve runs were below 29. What survives is weaker and is the whole point: eight green runs in hunt 1 read above the red run’s own reading, twelve more ran green ending at 235, and no per-run figure supports load as the variable. The "load 29" attributed to the red run is itself an after-the-fact reading of a ramp, not a measurement during it. NEXT: keep the instrument, and let the next natural occurrence name the role before any repair is attempted. The 2000 ms is an absolute on the admission-offer path and is where to look once the role is known.

next_action: NOTHING IN THE TREE IS BLOCKED AND NOTHING IS HALF-DONE. Tasks 21, 22 and 24’s instrument all landed this session; 24 stays OPEN by its own rule — one redness in twenty-two runs, load not established as the variable, so the next move is to let a natural occurrence name the role rather than to write a cause. Everything hosted remains deploy-gated and the gate is the owner’s: Cloudflare billing alert FIRST, then the first deploy. THE DEPLOY IS TWO DEPLOYS — ANNOUNCE_MULTIADDRS ships empty on purpose and hostedAddresses REFUSES an empty list, so the first deploy names the workers.dev subdomain and the second carries the address. Costed 2026-08-26 from published rates, NOT measured: one always-on object is 331 776 GB-s against 400 000 included, i.e. $5/month and nothing over; the marginal always-on object is ~$4.15/month. Only ONE object is reachable today — worker.ts:299 passes the compile-time constant SERVED_BY = bootstrap-us — so the three-name ceiling of ~$12.4/month needs Phase 33. Owner has set a $15/month budget, which clears every figure above, so the yamux keepalive decision is NOT a cost decision and reverts to being about how fast a peer notices a dead path. The one number worth measuring on the first deploy is whether each inbound WebSocket frame bills as a request. Do not deploy, do not create remote resources, --dry-run only, never --remote.
